 Summary
 Nations League Group A4 - Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo
 Dan James has best chance of a goalless first half but is denied by Norway goalkeeper Egil Selvik
 Antonio Nusa breaks the deadlock before hour mark to put Norway in front
 Andreas Schjelderup doubles the lead shortly after to put Norway firmly in control in Oslo
 David Brooks pulls one back for Wales with 12 minutes left to play
 Erling Haaland seals victory for hosts from the penalty spot after Connor Roberts fouled Schjelderup in the box
 Wales finish Group A4 campaign against Portugal in Cardiff on Tuesday
 Live Reporting
 Ian Mitchelmore
 Most recent Most popular Until Tuesday night! published at 19:33 GMT 19:33 GMT 
 FT: Norway 3-1 Wales 
 Image source, PA Media So it was not to be for Craig Bellamy's side tonight, despite plenty of encouraging aspects before they fell behind.
 Wales will finish at the bottom of their group, although all hope is not lost.
 A positive result against group leaders Portugal in Cardiff on Tuesday night could yet prove pivotal as Wales seek to earn themselves a play-off to avoid being relegated from League A.
 But for the time being, thanks as ever for joining us.
 We'll see you again on Tuesday.

 Positives to take from disappointing defeat - Bellamy published at 19:31 GMT 19:31 GMT 
 FT: Norway 3-1 Wales 
 Image source, PA Media Wales boss Craig Bellamy speaking to BBC Match of the Day Wales: 
 "It was a good performance. I thought there were huge parts of the game where we played really well.
 "We wanted to take the game to Norway here, we didn't want to just sit back.
 "I thought we could have been better with our final ball at times. I always felt we were in the game.
 "It could have been better, especially in the first half.
 "It was just that period after half time, we just dropped in our intensity a bit, and I can understand it as well.
 "We were able to make a few substitutions and we were able to flip it again.
 "Then we concede a goal which was very unlike a player who has been incredible for us, and for me. But overall, there were some things that were really positive.
 "I'd like to have this game again because there was some really good stuff out there at times, but it's still disappointing because we lost at the end of the day."
 1 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We have to put things right' - Ampadu published at 19:28 GMT 19:28 GMT 
 FT: Norway 3-1 Wales 
 Wales midfielder Ethan Ampadu speaking to BBC Match of the Day Wales: 
 "It is obviously disappointing. We have to put things right, we want to do better. 
 "We believe that we can come to places like this and show that we're a good team and it's just a bit more consistency to get a different result tonight.
 "Bellamy has obviously given us confidence and belief that we showed in spells. It's just about trying to do that more often and obviously to have the faith to keep believing.
 "We showed some good stuff and create a lot of chances so then we have to do that on Tuesday. 
 "Whenever you have that many chances, you want to score more goals, we have full belief that we can do that, so it's not too much to moan about now. It is about making sure that we can put that right on Tuesday against another very good team."
 Image source, Getty Images 
 3 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Tough result to take - James published at 19:25 GMT 19:25 GMT 
 FT: Norway 3-1 Wales 
 Wales winger Dan James speaking to BBC Match of the Day Wales: 
 "It was a tough one to take. We've come to a country that has been great, they've been in incredible form at home.
 "We tried to push to get something out of it, and I think it was very even. I think it was about who got the first goal.
 "I think we still stuck to our principles, played some great football and tried to work our way up the pitch.
 "It was frustrating to concede the second one, but Brooksy scored an unbelievable goal.
 "I think it was a tough one to take. Credit to the boys, I thought we were really good today against a good side, but we just fell short.
 "We had a great win at home, but these are a side that have beaten many teams. They got to the quarter-finals of the World Cup and they've got incredible players.
 "For 60 minutes it was very even, but as I said, it was about that first goal.
 "We've got another really important game on Tuesday so we've just got to get ready for that."
 Image source, Getty Images

 FULL-TIME - Norway 3-1 Wales published at 18:55 GMT 18:55 GMT 
 It's all over, and after an encouraging hour or so, it somewhat fell apart in the final 30 minutes - despite a brief Welsh fightback - as Norway took their chances.
 So ultimately, Norway claim revenge for the loss in Cardiff a month ago, and Craig Bellamy's side sit at the bottom of their Nations League group.
 They can no longer finish above Stale Solbakken's side given that Norway now have a better head-to-head record.
 Given that they also have an inferior head-to-head record with Denmark, Wales are now guaranteed to finish bottom.
 It does not mean they are relegated though. They could yet end as one of the best finishing fourth-placed sides in the top tier of the competition, which would mean they would enter a relegation play-off rather than instantly dropping into League B.

 next page Figure caption, Highlights: Norway beat Wales in Oslo
 By Dafydd Pritchard BBC Sport Wales in Oslo Wales' hopes of retaining their top-tier status in the Nations League are hanging in the balance after they were beaten by Norway in Oslo. 
 Craig Bellamy's side shaded a goalless first half in which they created the better chances, but Norway scored with their first shot on target as Antonio Nusa drilled in from the edge of the penalty area after an hour.
 The World Cup quarter-finalists doubled their lead nine minutes later as Nusa and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland combined for substitute Andreas Schjelderup to tap in.
 Wales kept themselves in the contest as David Brooks came off the bench to score with a delicate chipped finish, only for Haaland's penalty to wrap up victory for the hosts after Schjelderup was fouled by Connor Roberts.
 By avenging their defeat in Cardiff a month ago, Norway leapfrog Wales into third place in Group A4, meaning Bellamy's men will finish bottom.
 Even if they win their final game at home to group leaders and reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday, Wales cannot overtake Norway or Denmark - who are both three points ahead - because of their inferior head-to-head record.
 As a result, they are almost certain to face a relegation play-off against a League B team in March.
 Wales analysis: Promising display but no reward 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, David Brooks scored Wales' third goal of their Nations League campaign
 Wales earned their first win at this level when they deservedly beat Norway at home a month ago, but despite promising signs in Oslo, they remain without an away victory against a team ranked above them since beating Israel during Euro 2016 qualifying 11 years ago.
 Bellamy vowed before this encounter that his team would be going "all out" for victory regardless of their opponents' potency; Wales posed the greater threat of the two sides during the first half.
 Daniel James, Brennan Johnson and Harry Wilson all looked dangerous on the break, with James twice shooting wide after being set up by Wilson, before forcing Norway goalkeeper Egil Selvik into the first save of the game.
 This was an assured display from Wales, who were also disciplined and alert defensively as they contained their star-studded hosts.
 That was until the hour mark when their inability to properly clear a Norway corner presented Nusa - the hosts' sharpest player on the night - with the chance to fire in the goal his electric display on the left wing had warranted.
 Norway's individual star quality was on show as they doubled their advantage and, even with Brooks' deft finish, it was a long way back for Wales.
 Disappointing as it obviously will be for Bellamy and his players to finish bottom of their group, a probable relegation play-off presents them with a second chance to stay in the top division of the Nations League.
 What this result also means, however, is that Wales will now not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.

 Norway analysis: Revenge for Cardiff defeat 
 Norway had viewed this game as a chance to right some wrongs, not only the defeat by Wales in last month's reverse fixture but also the fact they had lost three successive matches for the first time in a decade.
 Having gone through 2025 unbeaten and caught the eye on their way to the quarter-finals of this summer's World Cup, this golden generation of Haaland, Martin Odegaard and others had been expected to compete for top spot at the start of this Nations League campaign.
 However, they started the evening at the bottom of Group A4 with just one win from four games, level with third-placed Wales on three points but below them because of their head-to-head record.
 There was a hint of frustration from the expectant home crowd at half-time but, once Nusa put Norway in front, they never looked like squandering their advantage.
 Haaland, who was shackled in Cardiff, was by no means at his devastating best, but he was still clinical enough to end the game with an assist and a remarkable 66th international goal from just 60 caps.
